analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The patch adds one bullet at head line 1025 (outside the supplied excerpts): App Attest serving authorization can stay visible through its unexpired lease, while MDM-removal advice needs a matching fresh coordinator decision, and this applies to both doctor summaries. It links to ../reference/provider-authorization.md. The change is documentation-only: no code, config defaults, key handling, endpoints or trust boundaries change. I could not see the added line, only the patch excerpt, and could not verify the linked doc or the doctor implementation. The wording is consistent with the TB-011 and T-057 posture (premature MDM removal, expiry and revocation). Being conservative, it does not loosen advice, and it separates lease visibility from removal guidance. That is a documentation correctness point, not a regression. I also reviewed the supplied base and head text of the CLI reference (cache, add-on runtime, App Attest evidence report, environment passthrough, SSD prefix-cache description). It is unchanged context and matches the retained threat model (T-041 SSD cache, TB-012 add-on socket, A-008 logout). No new attack surface or invalidated assumptions found. Remaining question for integration: whether the doctor code behavior matches the new sentence. That is outside the supplied evidence and is a documentation-accuracy concern.
